You're Richer Than 99% and Losing Anyway
description:
For thirty years, global inequality has been collapsing faster than at any point in human history — and you still feel poorer than your parents did. Both of those facts are drawn on the same chart, and one of them has been quietly hiding the other.


KEY TAKEAWAYS:
• Extreme poverty fell from 38% of humanity in 1990 to under 10% today, and the global Gini dropped from roughly 0.70 to the low 0.60s — the first sustained fall since the Industrial Revolution.
• The same decades ran in reverse inside rich countries: the US top 1% wealth share climbed from about 24% in 1989 to roughly 31% now. Two curves crossed, and nobody announced it.
• In 1975 the world had two income humps — a poor-world hump and a rich-world hump. By 2015 they had fused into one. The rich world's floor now sits inside the global middle.
• From 1988 to 2008, the flattest real income gains on Earth belonged not to the poorest, but to the 80th–90th global percentile: the Western working and lower-middle class. That flat stretch is the trunk of the elephant — and it's you.
